chunks: Our father and Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluyih (may God be pleased with them) narrated, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Imran al-Ash'ari narrated to us, from some of our companions, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali and Abi al-Sakhr, both of whom linked it up to the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him).

That he said: 'Traveling (for pilgrimage) is not to be undertaken except to three mosques: The Sacred Mosque (Al-Haram), the Mosque of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family), and the Mosque of Kufa.'
ai.seo_question: Which three mosques are designated for special travel in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal* establishes the principle of *ziyarat* (visitation) by specifying three mosques as primary destinations for devotional travel, notably elevating the Mosque of Kufa to the same status as the two holiest sites in Islam. This inclusion reflects the unique Shia emphasis on Kufa as a central hub of Imam Ali’s authority and the early Islamic community, distinguishing it from the Sunni tradition which typically recognizes only Mecca and Medina. The ruling underscores the spiritual merit attached to physically connecting with sites of historical and religious significance in Shia jurisprudence.
